newsitem.title: INDIA: Demand for imported metals seen rising in India.
newsitem.headline: Demand for imported metals seen rising in India.

text.p: Business in base metals on Indian markets is expected to pick up in the current week as industrial demand increases for imported stock, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said a recent firm world trend had prompted local producers to raise prices, giving traders who had earlier imported metals at lower prices an edge in the market.
"Now traders are booking profits," said Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) and Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL), both state-owned, have raised prices for June after a recent firm trend in base metals on the London Metals Exchange (LME).
Prices for HCL's copper wire bar and rod were raised by 6,000 rupees per tonne to 14,260 and 14,950 rupees respectively, dealers said.
Market prices of copper wire bar and rods were around 13,700/13,750 and 14,500 rupees per tonne, dealers said.
"Buyers are coming to the market as dealers could afford to offer stocks at relatively lower prices," Parikh said. "I expect the local market to firm in the current week."
In the week to Wednesday, nickel and tin suffered losses following a slide in global prices. Nickel lost 600 rupees to 36,400 rupees per quintal and tin 200 rupees to 31,200 rupees per quintal.
Copper, however, gained 75 to 13,700/13,750. Zinc rose 50 to 8,050.
Aluminium was up 50 at 7,700 while lead was down 50 at 4,100.
Dealers said they expected local aluminium producers also to raise prices in view of a firm world trend.
But in London, aluminium traders reported an easing of recent tight supply, which contributed to a price fall of $18 on Tuesday to a six-week low of $1,578 a tonne on the LME.
In Bombay, business was dull on Wednesday as dealers were cautious after a 40-million rupee payment default last week had shaken their confidence.
"When traders become cautious, a liquidity crunch grips the market. This normally happens after every payment default," said a dealer.
